correctness.rationale: Every finite-field algebra endomorphism is a substitution of generators by nilpotents. An invertible tangent map is an automorphism by the nilpotent filtration; conjugating an idempotent to its tangent projection uses \(h(u)=e(u)\), \(h(w)=w-e(w)\). Among tangent-identity automorphisms, there are \(q^{nH_d(n)}\) total and \(q^{rH_d(r)+(n-r)H_d(n)}\) stabilizing a fixed coordinate image, yielding \(q^{r(H_d(n)-H_d(r))}\) images per tangent r-plane. A fixed image admits \(q^{(n-r)(r+H_d(r))}\) retractions by freely assigning complementary generators inside its maximal ideal. Thus both formulas follow for all \(n\ge1,d\ge2\),prime powers q. Exhaustive substitution computations for (n,d,q)=(2,3,2),(2,3,3),(2,4,2),(3,2,2),(3,2,3) plus a separate \(\mathbb F_4\) matrix enumeration independently verify image counts, uniform fibers and total retractions in those finite cases; finite tests are not a substitute for the general proof.

value.rationale: The collection of embedded retract images and the number of idempotent algebra endomorphisms realizing any specified image are natural invariants of a finite algebra endomorphism monoid. The formulas completely determine both for all finite fields, generator dimensions and nilpotence lengths, including higher nonlinear jets where square-zero linear-algebra counting no longer suffices. Unlike a single scalar total, the uniform-fiber theorem supplies full image/fiber distribution and exact counts for embedded subalgebras. This is motivated by quantitative refinements of the structural retract classification; it does not claim coordinate normal form as new.
